description: FirstMate Data Privacy & Classification Policy V3. Five payload-based classes; SECRET is the only absolute exclusion; opencode_go gates PERSONAL_SENSITIVE per concrete model via config/provider-privacy-metadata.json instead of one blanket profile claim.

PUBLIC.description: Open source code, public documentation, published packages, public web content.

SANITIZED.description: De-identified logs, scrubbed snippets with no PII, tokens, keys, or personal identifying traits.

PRIVATE_CODE.description: Unpublished or proprietary source code and technical content with no personal-sensitive payload - e.g. a Gabriel OS code-only task. Classify by the actual payload, not by the repository it lives in: living in a personal repo does not by itself make a payload PERSONAL_SENSITIVE.

PERSONAL_SENSITIVE.description: Personal journals, daily habits, personal finances, personal memory (Gabriel OS atomic facts), unshared thoughts, and other genuinely personal-sensitive payloads. Supersedes v2's PERSONAL_PRIVATE and SHARED_TRAMPOLIM, both folded here as a conservative simplification (see docs/router-v3-wp2-data-policy-port.md).
PERSONAL_SENSITIVE.note: opencode_go allows this class structurally, but each concrete model additionally requires verified per-model privacy metadata (config/provider-privacy-metadata.json) confirming no training use and zero retention; a missing or stale entry fails closed.

SECRET.description: API keys, private SSH keys, master passwords, OAuth refresh tokens, credentials, seed phrases.
SECRET.note: Secrets must never be sent to any LLM prompt, context window, or external API, under any provider. This is the only absolute exclusion left in the policy.

opencode_go.note: This gateway proxies many unrelated vendors (OpenAI, xAI, Zhipu, Moonshot, Meta, Alibaba, DeepSeek, and others). The v2 blanket claim ("vendor_disallow_on_proxy" / "transient_gateway") was measurably wrong for Grok 4.6, GPT-5.6 Luna (30-day retention), and Muse Spark models (training-enabled). PERSONAL_SENSITIVE now requires a passing per-model check against config/provider-privacy-metadata.json; see docs/router-v3-wp2-data-policy-port.md for the live re-fetched evidence.

rules: Privacy constraints always outrank model capability, latency, and spare quota.
SECRET is strictly stripped and excluded from all model context under any provider - the only absolute exclusion.
Classify the actual payload, not the repository or task it came from - a personal repo does not make a code-only payload PERSONAL_SENSITIVE by default; use PRIVATE_CODE.
PERSONAL_SENSITIVE is allowed on claude_consumer, codex_consumer, and (per-model-gated) opencode_go under training opt-out / verified zero-retention.
opencode_go's PERSONAL_SENSITIVE allowance requires a fresh, passing per-model entry in config/provider-privacy-metadata.json; missing or stale metadata fails closed.
China-hosted models (opencode_go_cn) are hard-blocked on PERSONAL_SENSITIVE and SECRET.
